target_customer: developers and automation teams at enterprises, mainly in Brazil and Latin America at founding, now global
problem: RPA tools were low-code and locked-in; developers wanted code-based automation. Later: AI-generated Python scripts proliferate without governance.
business_model: software platform (orchestration, observability, governance) on an open-source core; pricing not found

founders.name: Lorhan Caproni
education: Molecular Biology and Administration (per YC page)

founders.name: Gabriel Archanjo
prior_employers: Game studio working with Nintendo and Sega platforms (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: About 15 years as developer, tech lead and CTO.

competitors.name: UiPath
competitors.traction_then: customers incl. Google, DHL, Equifax; US$221M revenue in the latest quarter

technical_complexity.rationale: Computer-vision desktop automation plus orchestration for a team of two engineers; standard engineering with hard parts in robustness.

defensibility.rationale: Open-source core and developer focus differentiate, but incumbents had far more resources; deployed automations may create lock-in once in production.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not buy BotCity; the company stayed independent and raised a US$12M round in 2025 after pivoting its pitch to AI-script governance.

market_need_then: VentureBeat (2022-02) cited RPA market of US$1.61B in 2020 projected to US$7.64B by 2028; the CEO argued developers need code-based tooling beyond low-code RPA.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, mission-driven, optimistic; 'innovation and control' (company blog 2025)

branding.community_and_virality: Open-source framework and a company blog (open-source RPA post, 2023); no evidence of merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Developer-community and open-source presence plus 1,000+ production teams per its own blog, but no independent press about the brand.

pivots.from: developer-first RPA built on computer vision
pivots.to: observability and governance for AI-generated Python scripts
pivots.why: Company frames it as governing automations created by AI (2025 funding post); the dated shift itself is inferred from that post and the YC one-liner.

outcome_analysis: BotCity, a Brazilian developer-first RPA company, raised a US$2.5M seed in December 2021 (SoftBank Latin America and Astella) plus a US$500K YC extension, then a US$12M round in September 2025 led by Four Rivers while repositioning toward governing AI-generated scripts. The company reports over 1,000 teams in production with customers such as Bayer and LG. It survived against much larger RPA incumbents; the traction figures are self-reported.
